identity.name: Goths
alt_names: Goths of Scandza and the Vistula

land.text: the Goths' lands on the Vistula and Bug, then 'Scythia', 'roughly in modern Ukraine' (Oium page); Cliopatria's Gothia row opens in 207 between the Dniester and the Dnieper

successors.note: The Goths page has the Wielbark culture shift 'southeast towards the Black Sea' from the middle of the 2nd century and contribute to the Chernyakhov culture 'by the mid-3rd century'; the 206/207 handover is Cliopatria's row boundary, not a dated event.

keyframe_review.note: 97,393 km2 in Sweden (Gotaland), 30-42: Jordanes' homeland Scandza before the migration. The Gothiscandza page dates the migration 'to the first half of the 1st century CE' while warning that Jordanes' reliability 'has been called into question'; the Goths page says 'scholars who accept a Scandinavian origin describe gradual migration in the 1st centuries BC and AD'. No page places a Gothic polity in Sweden in these years, so the shape stands only as the traditional homeland, soft. No page opened gives an infobox area to compare.

correction.text: only the Vistula-mouth lobe: 'in the 1st century the mouth of the Vistula was indicated as the land of the Gutones'; the Wielbark culture 'emerged in the lower Vistula and along the Pomeranian coast in the 1st century'

keyframe_review.note: 117,739 km2 in Cliopatria for 43-153 is two lobes: Gotaland in Sweden (about 119,000 km2 of cells) and a Vistula-mouth lobe in Poland (about 21,700 km2). After the Gothiscandza landing ('first half of the 1st century CE') the pages place the Gutones only on the Vistula: Pliny (AD 77) and Tacitus (c. 98) name them in Germania, Ptolemy (c. 150) puts them 'east of the Vistula' (Gutones page); nothing opened keeps a Gothic state in Sweden. The Wielbark culture also 'stretched southwards, into the region around Poznan' in the 1st-2nd centuries (Wielbark page), a soft margin not drawn here.

75,478 km2, 154-196, central and south-east Poland to Volhynia: 'Beginning in the middle of the 2nd century, the Wielbark culture shifted southeast towards the' Black Sea (Goths page). The shape leaves the Pomeranian coast, where 'isolated pockets of the Wielbark culture persisted in northern Poland until the 5th century' (Wielbark page); those are not a Gothic state. No infobox area on the pages opened.
The same 75,478 km2 outline for 197-206. 'By 200 AD' the Wielbark Goths were 'probably in Roman service' (Goths page); the move to the Black Sea is next in Gothia (207).

region.text: Scandza, the Goths' homeland in Jordanes' account

ledger.note: 30: the Goths appear in Scandza, their homeland in Jordanes' account. The year is Cliopatria's; no page dates a Gothic state, and the Gutones are first named by Pliny in AD 77 and Tacitus c. 98 (Gutones page).

region.text: Scandza, left in the migration under King Berig

ledger.note: 43: the Goths leave Scandza for the Vistula. 'The migration is dated to the first half of the 1st century CE' (Gothiscandza page); 43 is Cliopatria's year inside that bracket, and a gradual migration across the 1st centuries BC and AD is the other reading (Goths page).

region.text: Gothiscandza, 'the first settlement area of the Goths after their migration from Scandza', at the mouth of the Vistula

ledger.note: 43: the Goths land at Gothiscandza on the Vistula mouth. 'As soon as they had set foot in the land, they named the area Gothiscandza'; the Ulmerugi 'had arrived in the area already before the Goths' and were chased off, then 'they defeated their new neighbours, the Vandals' (Jordanes via the Gothiscandza page, undated). The Ulmerugi are the Rugii of Jordanes, not the later Rugiland.

region.text: the Pomeranian coast and lower Vistula left by the Cliopatria shape

ledger.note: 154: the coastal homeland drops out of the Gothic shape as the people move south-east. 'Isolated pockets of the Wielbark culture persisted in northern Poland until the 5th century' (Wielbark page); the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the south-east: the Vistula and Bug towards Volhynia and the upper Dniester

ledger.note: 154: the Goths move south-east towards the Black Sea. 'Beginning in the middle of the 2nd century, the Wielbark culture shifted southeast towards the' Black Sea; the Wielbark page adds that it 'expanded southwards along the Vistula and Bug towards the upper Dniester' in the first half of the 3rd century. The page names no people displaced, so the counterpart is nobody.

region.text: the Goths' lands on the Vistula and Bug

ledger.note: 206: the Goths pass into Gothia on the Black Sea steppe. Oium, 'a name for Scythia, or a fertile part of it, roughly in modern Ukraine', is where Jordanes has the Goths settle under Filimer, undated; the Goths page has Wielbark contribute to the Chernyakhov culture 'by the mid-3rd century'. The 206/207 boundary is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Gothic conquest of Gothiscandza (Jordanes' account)
wars.outcome: In Jordanes' story the Goths chased the Rugians from the Vistula mouth and then 'defeated their new neighbours, the Vandals'; the page dates only the migration, 'the first half of the 1st century CE', and doubts Jordanes' reliability.
wars.note: Years 1-50 are the page's bracket for the migration, not dates of fighting; no zone is drawn because no page dates a conquest or names its land beyond the Vistula mouth.

certainty.note: A people on the move, known from Greco-Roman ethnography and archaeological cultures; no frontier is recorded. The Scandza shape of 30-42 is a traditional homeland (Jordanes), the Vistula and Bug shapes follow the Wielbark culture.

sources.title: Goths
sources.note: Origins (Gutones on the Vistula in the 1st century, Jordanes' Scandza), the Wielbark shift south-east from the mid-2nd century, 'by 200 AD', the Chernyakhov link.

sources.title: Wielbark culture
sources.note: Emergence at Gdansk and Chelmno in the 1st century, expansion to Poznan and the upper Dniester, pockets to the 5th century.

sources.title: Gutones
sources.note: Attestations: Pliny AD 77, Tacitus c. 98, Ptolemy c. 150 east of the Vistula.

sources.title: Oium
sources.note: Jordanes' Scythia of the Goths, roughly modern Ukraine; no date.

sources.title: Gothiscandza
sources.note: The Berig migration dated to the first half of the 1st century CE; Ulmerugi and Vandals; Vistula mouth.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Goths' (30-206) is a people, not a state with a government: no page opened names a king, a capital or a border, so identity.capitals is empty and no ruler strip is given (Berig and Filimer are Jordanes' undated figures). The dossier keeps Cliopatria's life span because the Goths dossier is the lead-in to Gothia (207-382), and the map should show the Scandza-Vistula-Black Sea story; the start year 30 and end year 206 are Cliopatria's (found and dissolve at confidence 1).

Disputed: the Scandinavian origin. The Goths page has Greco-Roman sources first attesting the Gutones near the lower Vistula in the 1st century, and says only scholars who accept a Scandinavian origin describe a gradual migration in the 1st centuries BC and AD; the Gothiscandza page puts the migration in the first half of the 1st century CE and doubts Jordanes. The Sweden lobe of the 30-153 shapes is therefore soft; the dossier keeps it for 30-42 (the homeland before the landing) and removes it from 43 (verdict adjust on goths_43). The first-century Gutones are 'near the lower Vistula' in every dated attestation (Pliny 77, Tacitus c. 98, Ptolemy c. 150).

Counterparts: the Ulmerugi (Rugii) of Jordanes' story are not the Rugiland of 455-489; no Cliopatria row covers the Vistula's earlier peoples (Oksywie, Przeworsk, Vandals, Gepids). No infobox area exists on any page opened, so the factor-of-two check against Cliopatria's areas was impossible. Gothia (207-382) is the continuation; a Chernyakhov-culture-based dossier is not needed.
